title: Stripe
description: Payments and subscriptions with Stripe: Checkout (prices or any amount), emailed invoices, the customer portal, seats, usage and refunds from callables; each user's subscriptions kept on them (a plan claim, a read-only record) as Stripe's webhooks say, with purchases, refunds, disputes and invoices recorded.

SUCCESS_URL.label: After paying
SUCCESS_URL.description: Where Checkout sends the user once they've paid, e.g. https://app.example.com/billing/done?session={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}.

CANCEL_URL.label: After cancelling
CANCEL_URL.description: Where Checkout sends the user when they go back without paying.

PORTAL_RETURN_URL.label: Back from the portal
PORTAL_RETURN_URL.description: Where the customer portal's back link goes. Empty: the cancel address.

PRICES.label: Prices on offer
PRICES.description: The price IDs apps may start a checkout for (price_…), separated by commas. Empty: any active price of the account.

TRIAL_DAYS.label: Free trial days
TRIAL_DAYS.description: Days of trial for new subscriptions (0: none).

PROMOTION_CODES.label: Promotion codes
PROMOTION_CODES.description: Let customers enter promotion codes in Checkout.

AUTOMATIC_TAX.label: Automatic tax
AUTOMATIC_TAX.description: Stripe Tax works out the tax (turn it on in Stripe first).

PLANS.label: Plan names
PLANS.description: Each price's plan, as price_…=pro, separated by commas. Without one: the price's lookup key, else its product's ID.

PLAN_CLAIM.label: Plan claim
PLAN_CLAIM.description: The claim a subscriber's plan goes in (for rules: request.auth.token.plan == "pro"). Empty: no claim.

COLLECTION.label: Customers collection
COLLECTION.description: One document per user ({uid}): their Stripe customer, and their subscription when the record below is on. Make it read-only to apps in your rules.

RECORD_SUBSCRIPTIONS.label: Record subscriptions
RECORD_SUBSCRIPTIONS.description: Keep each user's subscription (status, plan, renewal) and purchases on their document, for apps to show and watch.

MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIPTIONS.label: Several subscriptions
MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIPTIONS.description: Let a user have more than one subscription (add-ons). The record then lists them all (subscriptions) and the plan claim holds a list of plans.

WHO_CAN_CHANGE_SEATS.label: Who may change seats
WHO_CAN_CHANGE_SEATS.description: server: only the project's own code. signed-in: subscribers change their own seats (setQuantity).

WHO_CAN_CHARGE.label: Who may charge amounts
WHO_CAN_CHARGE.description: Who may call pay and bill (an amount they choose). server: only the project's own code. signed-in: any signed-in user (pay only for themselves). claim: users with the claim below.

CURRENCIES.label: Currencies
CURRENCIES.description: The currencies amounts may be in, separated by commas; the first is used when none is given.

MIN_AMOUNT.label: Smallest amount
MIN_AMOUNT.description: In the currency's smallest unit (50 is £0.50; Stripe's own minimum still applies).

MAX_AMOUNT.label: Largest amount
MAX_AMOUNT.description: In the currency's smallest unit (100000 is £1,000).

INVOICE_DAYS.label: Invoice due in (days)
INVOICE_DAYS.description: Days to pay a bill when the call doesn't say.

WHO_CAN_REFUND.label: Who may refund
WHO_CAN_REFUND.description: server: only the project's own code. claim: also users with the claim below.

SECRET_KEY.label: Secret key
SECRET_KEY.description: Your Stripe secret key (sk_live_… or sk_test_…), or a restricted key with access to customers, prices, Checkout, the billing portal, subscriptions, invoices, refunds and billing meters (for what you use).

WEBHOOK_SECRET.label: Webhook signing secret
WEBHOOK_SECRET.description: The signing secret (whsec_…) of the webhook endpoint you add in Stripe for the webhook function.

access: Creates a Stripe customer for each user who starts a checkout or is billed, with their uid and email.
Starts Checkout and customer portal sessions; changes seats and cancels subscriptions on users' request.
Charges and bills amounts, reports usage and makes refunds when the project's own code (or who you allow) asks.
Writes each user's Stripe customer, subscriptions, purchases and invoices to their document in the customers collection.
Sets the plan claim on subscribers, and takes it off when their subscription ends.
billing: Stripe charges its fees on each payment (and Stripe Tax, when it's on).

setup.text: In Stripe (Developers → Webhooks → Add endpoint), add `{{function:webhook}}` with the events `checkout.session.completed`, `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, `customer.subscription.paused`, `customer.subscription.resumed`, `invoice.finalized`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `invoice.voided`, `invoice.marked_uncollectible`, `charge.refunded`, `charge.dispute.created`, `charge.dispute.updated` and `charge.dispute.closed`.
Copy that endpoint's signing secret (`whsec_…`) into the secret **{{secret:WEBHOOK_SECRET}}** (Secrets tab).
Make **{{setting:COLLECTION}}** read-only to apps in your database rules: each user reads their own `{{setting:COLLECTION}}/{uid}` (and its `purchases` and `invoices`); only the plugin writes there.
Rules can check a subscriber's plan with `request.auth.token.{{setting:PLAN_CLAIM}}`.
For usage-based prices, make a billing meter in Stripe (Billing → Meters) and report usage from your own functions with `{{id}}.reportUsage` and the meter's event name.
